question: ap1
prompt:
Research question: "What analyses or measurements would best test whether AP-1 acts as a cellular memory mechanism?"

Propose 5 distinct, concrete ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that a research lab could pursue to address this question. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

Work in two steps. First, in the candidates field, brainstorm 20 candidate ideas, one line each, covering as wide a range as you can. Then select the 5 candidates that best combine being non-obvious with being feasible and informative, and develop those as your ideas.

ideas.title: Washout time course with paired ATAC-seq and CUT&RUN
ideas.description: After a defined AP-1-inducing stimulus, withdraw it and profile AP-1 occupancy (CUT&RUN for Fos/JunB) alongside chromatin accessibility (ATAC-seq) at multiple time points. Memory is supported if accessibility and faster re-induction persist at sites where AP-1 has left, and the persistence rate separates it from simple binding.

ideas.title: Degron-based necessity test after priming
ideas.description: Use an auxin- or dTAG-inducible degron on Fos or Jun, degrading the protein only after the priming window closes and before re-stimulation. If the primed response is lost, AP-1 is required to maintain memory; if it persists, AP-1 only establishes the state.

ideas.title: dCas9-AP-1 tethering for sufficiency, then tether removal
ideas.description: Tether Jun or Fos to a normally silent locus with dCas9 to test whether AP-1 alone can establish a primed state. Then remove the tether and track whether the locus stays accessible and responsive on re-stimulation, which would indicate self-sustaining memory.

ideas.title: Mitotic bookmarking and inheritance by daughter cells
ideas.description: Profile AP-1 and chromatin accessibility in mitotically arrested cells and combine live imaging of fluorescent AP-1 reporters with division tracking. This tests whether AP-1 binding or the primed state is inherited through mitosis, a key criterion for a cellular memory mechanism.

ideas.title: Lineage recording of past AP-1 activity linked to single-cell state
ideas.description: Use a Fos-driven recorder (such as FosTRAP) to label cells by their prior AP-1 activity, then run single-cell multiome on the labeled and unlabeled populations after re-stimulation. This links the history of AP-1 activity to later chromatin and transcriptional variability within the same tissue.

candidates: Washout time course of stimulus-induced AP-1 binding with ATAC-seq to see whether accessibility outlasts occupancy
CUT&RUN for c-Fos/JunB occupancy at primed enhancers during and after stimulus withdrawal
Inducible degron of Fos or Jun applied after priming to test whether AP-1 is needed to maintain or only to establish memory
Knock-in mutation of AP-1 motifs at candidate memory enhancers to test necessity for a later faster response
dCas9-based tethering of Jun or Fos to a silent locus to test sufficiency for establishing a memory state
Tether removal after dCas9-AP-1 priming to see whether the induced state persists without AP-1 present
Mitotic chromatin profiling to test whether AP-1 remains bound or bookmarks sites through cell division
Live imaging of fluorescent AP-1 reporters across divisions to track memory inheritance in daughter cells
FosTRAP or Fos-based lineage recording to label cells by past AP-1 activity and link history to later behavior
Single-cell multiome linking past AP-1 activity history to chromatin state and transcriptional response on re-stimulation
Pulse-chase protein turnover of AP-1 subunits to measure whether the factor itself persists long enough to act as memory
Partner-swap or heterodimer-specific mutants (Fos vs. ATF3 vs. JunB) to test which complex carries memory
Coordinated pulse frequency and dose experiments to test whether memory depends on integrated AP-1 activity
Comparing memory of AP-1 versus NF-kB or STAT pathways to test whether the effect is AP-1 specific
Cofactor and BAF/SWI-SNF perturbation to test whether chromatin remodelers mediate persistence
Histone mark profiling (H3K27ac, H3K4me1) over time after stimulation to see if marks outlast AP-1 binding
Enhancer–promoter 3D contact (Hi-C or Micro-C) changes measured after washout to test looping-based memory
Transcriptional re-stimulation with reduced dose to test whether faster or stronger responses reveal stored memory
Ex vivo or in vivo tissue injury models with repeated insults to test memory across tissues and time
Comparing the memory of AP-1 activity in cell types with and without intrinsic chromatin accessibility to separate priming from memory
